items.claim: CEO states Q4 FY26 guidance midpoint implies about 34% revenue growth for the year.
items.quote: that would put us at a growth rate of 34% for this year
items.speaker: Seamus Grady, CEO

items.claim: CEO states the company's growth rate up to 2025 was a 16% CAGR, distinct from the 19% FY25 and ~34% FY26 figures.
items.quote: we grew our compound annual growth rate was 16%.
items.speaker: Seamus Grady, CEO

items.claim: CEO states current OpEx is about 1.4% of revenue.
items.quote: Our OpEx right now is about 1.4%
items.speaker: Seamus Grady, CEO

items.claim: CFO states fixed cost is about 5% of revenue, which limits gross-margin leverage on the upside but protects margin on a growth slowdown.
items.quote: our fixed cost is about 5% of our revenue
items.speaker: Csaba Sverha, CFO

items.claim: CEO says a competitor would need roughly 20 years and significant experience to replicate Fabrinet's capability.
items.quote: about 20 years and a lot of experience
items.speaker: Seamus Grady, CEO

items.claim: CEO states Fabrinet makes up to 60-70% of the bill of materials in-house for some products, which it frames as a competitive and stickiness advantage.
items.quote: we make up to 60%, 70% of the bill of material in-house.
items.speaker: Seamus Grady, CEO

items.claim: CEO states Building 10 capex is about $132-133 million depending on FX.
items.quote: the CapEx is about $132 million, $133 million
items.speaker: Seamus Grady, CEO

items.claim: CEO states Building 10 is expected to generate about 40% ROIC at full run rate.
items.quote: the building will generate about 40% ROIC
items.speaker: Seamus Grady, CEO

items.claim: CEO states total owned land capacity across Thailand campuses supports about $12 billion of revenue.
items.quote: land capacity, let's say, for about $12 billion of revenue.
items.speaker: Seamus Grady, CEO

items.claim: CEO states the Raytek investment gives Fabrinet access to co-packaged optics and silicon photonics wafer-level packaging processes it lacked in-house.
items.quote: co-packaged optics and also for silicon photonics.
items.speaker: Seamus Grady, CEO

items.claim: CEO states Raytek will establish a manufacturing footprint on Fabrinet's Thailand campus in the coming quarters.
items.quote: Raytek will be establishing a manufacturing footprint
items.speaker: Seamus Grady, CEO

items.claim: CEO identifies laser supply, specifically EMLs, as a particular industry-wide supply pinch point he views as transient.
items.quote: particularly around laser supply, specifically EMLs
items.speaker: Seamus Grady, CEO

items.claim: CFO states free cash flow has seen pressure in the last two quarters from capital expansion and working capital build-out, expected to continue near-term.
items.quote: we have seen some pressure given the capital expansion
items.speaker: Csaba Sverha, CFO

items.claim: CEO lists Fabrinet's customer base as including NVIDIA and Cisco among others.
items.quote: Our customers range from companies like NVIDIA, Cisco,
items.speaker: Seamus Grady, CEO

items.claim: CEO states most large customers are now willingly giving Fabrinet 2 to 3 years of demand visibility, which is unusual for the industry.
items.quote: give us 2 years or maybe even up to 3 years of visibility
items.speaker: Seamus Grady, CEO

items.claim: CEO states the newly announced transceiver program wins will ramp over the next 12 to 18 months.
items.quote: We'll ramp those over the next 12 to 18 months
items.speaker: Seamus Grady, CEO

items.claim: CEO states the combination of two new transceiver customer wins, or possibly either one alone, could be as big as the existing NVIDIA business.
items.quote: either one of them could be as big as that.
items.speaker: Seamus Grady, CEO

qa_flags.question: How are you thinking about the OCS opportunity, and how soon can we see revenues relative to OCS products once engagements turn into wins?
qa_flags.response_pattern: CEO explicitly declines to opine on whether OCS is 'a winning product or not,' and does not address the 'how soon' revenue-timing part of the question at all, instead redirecting to general capability/comfort language ('very promising,' 'excited to work with a couple of our customers').
